{{Otheruses|Overlord}}
{{Youmay|Sith'ari|a [[Dark Lord prophecy|prophecy]] about the Dark Lords of the Sith}}
[[File:SithariProphecy-BoS.png|thumb|right|300px|The Sith'ari Prophecy recorded in the ''Book of Sith'']]
{{Quote|Some of the old texts speak of the Sith'ari. They say the Sith will one day be led by a perfect being, one who embodies the dark side and all we stand for.|[[Qordis]]|<ref name="DBPoD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref>}}
'''Sith'ari''' was an ancient title that, in [[Sith (language)|Sith]], meant "the [[Lord/Legends|Lord]]" or "[[Overlord]]." It was first claimed by the [[King/Legends|King]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] [[Adas]] who unified the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] twelve millennia before the formation of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].

After Adas's death, the term became the subject of a legend prophesying the coming of a being that would lead and destroy the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], but in doing so would make the Sith more powerful than ever before. In this context, the term came to mean "perfect being" or "god." The prophecy, which was in many ways similar to the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] prophecy of the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]], retained its importance for the Sith up until the time of the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Order of the Sith]].

==The Sith'ari Prophecy==
{{Quote|One who has freed themselves from all restrictions has reached perfection, their potential fulfilled. Perfect strength, perfect power, perfect destiny. Imagine it. That is our ideal, at any rate. It is said in Sith legend that the 'Sith'ari'... the perfect being... will one day lead us. But perhaps that is just a legend.|[[Yuthura Ban]]|<ref name="KotOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
Inspired by the legend of the ancient [[Sith King|King]] [[Adas]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]],<ref name="TCSWE">{{CSWECite|III|155|Sith'ari}}</ref> the Sith'ari legend prophesied the coming of the ultimate [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].<ref name="KotOR" /> This "perfect being" would rise to power and bring balance to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="TCSWE" /> Free of all restrictions, the Sith'ari would lead the Sith but, according to the prophecy, destroy them as well; yet, through their destruction, make them stronger than ever.<ref name="BoSSftDS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> In that respect , the term of Sith'ari came to mean Immortal God-King.<ref name="Despoilers">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-3|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 3|nolive=1}}</ref>

The Sith'ari Prophecy was considered too sacred to be put into writing by the [[Kissai]], who passed it on verbally from generation to generation. Eventually, the ''[[Jen'jidai]]'' [[Sorzus Syn]] recorded it thus:<ref name="BoSSftDS" />
<poem>
''The Sith'ari will be free of limits.''
''The Sith'ari will lead the Sith and destroy them.''
''The Sith'ari will raise the Sith from death and make them stronger than before.''
</poem>

The prophecy was to a large extent similar to the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] prophecy of the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]], reflecting the need of a savior for both groups.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

==History==
===Adas, the first Sith'ari===
[[File:Adas.jpg|thumb|right|King Adas, the first Sith'ari]]
{{Quote|While some among the Kissai priests deem that the prophecy began and ended with Adas, many more await the Sith'ari{{'s}} return.|[[Sorzus Syn]]|<ref name="BoSSftDS" />}}
Sith'ari, meaning "the Lord" or "[[Overlord]]" in [[Sith (language)|Sith language]], was a title originally assumed by [[Adas]], the [[Sith King|King]]  of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] after he unified the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith people]] under his rule in the [[Pre-Republic era]].<ref name="ENDTSD">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref>

After the death of Adas during the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Invasion of Korriban]]<ref name="ENDTSD" /> around [[27,700 BBY]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|Sith Kingdom]] fragmented. Without the stabilizing influence of Adas, a [[Korriban civil war|civil war]] erupted on Korriban. The Sith battled against each other for rule of their people, with the reigning combatants arrogantly claiming
the title of Sith'ari.<ref name="ENDTSD" /> The Kingdom of the Sith remained largely fragmented for the next millennia<ref name="KPoLS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002korriban|text=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|int=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls}}</ref> but the title of Sith'ari remained a key tenet of Sith lore.<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 04: King Adas}}</ref>

===The legend===
{{Quote|Prophecies are generally wishful thinking ... The fact that the Sith created their own savior myth is predictable ... [Yet these predictions] seem uniquely specific to the actions I am taking now ... I am not a creature of superstition. But if the robes of the Sith'ari ["perfect being"] fit, I see no reason not to claim them. |[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]|<ref name="BoSSftDS" />}}
The prophecy of the Sith'ari appeared during the millennia that followed the death of King Adas and the fragmentation of the Kingdom of the Sith.<ref name="ENDTSD" /> In [[6900 BBY]], <ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> a group of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] from the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] [[Discovery of Korriban|arrived]] on Korriban. Led by [[Ajunta Pall]], the [[Exiles]] quickly subdued the Sith and Pall became the first [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], paving the way for the creation of the first [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="ENDTSD" /> One of the Exiles, [[Sorzus Syn]], discovered the legend of the Sith'ari and was the first to write it, breaking the old rule of exclusive oral transmission.<ref name="BoSSftDS" />

Over the next millennia, the legend of the Sith'ari remained strong in the Sith society and persisted despite the collapses and resurgences of Sith Empires. It was well known among the [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith acolytes]] of the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] of Korriban at the time of [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire]] and at the time of the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]].<ref name="KotOR" /><ref name="DBPoD" /> Nevertheless, not all Sith believed to the prophecy.<ref name="DBPoD" />

During the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] era, [[Darth Andeddu]] claimed the title of Sith'ari of [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]].<ref name="Despoilers" />

[[File:DarthBane-DoE.png|thumb|left|[[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], the foretold Sith'ari.]]
During the [[New Sith Wars]], [[Kopecz]] stated his belief that the new student at the Academy known as [[Darth Bane/Legends|Bane]] might be the Sith'ari, given how incredibly strong the young man was in the Force. Some of the other students on Korriban thought Bane's rival, [[Sirak]], was the Sith'ari. However, Sirak was killed by Bane. Darth Bane, eventually becoming a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], finally fulfilled the prophecy in many ways, first by providing [[Skere Kaan]] with the [[thought bomb]], which caused the annihilation of the Brotherhood of Darkness, and then by instating the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]],<ref name="DBPoD" /> leading to a [[Order of the Sith Lords|powerful line]] of Sith by reducing their numbers to only two at a time. This allowed the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] to distill in two vessels only; whereas Bane believed that its power in the past had been spread far too thin among the vast numbers of Sith 'lords'. This concentration of strength also made it easier to hide the Sith until they built up enough power to destroy the Jedi Order, and thereby open the way for the Sith to rule the galaxy.<ref name="BoSSftDS" /> Many Sith would later consider Bane as the Sith'ari.<ref name="TJP" />

The legend retained its significance for the Sith after the fall of the Sith Empires and the establishment of Darth Bane's Rule of Two. According to [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]], Darth Bane was the foretold Sith'ari.<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> Although [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], due to being a creature of logic and not superstition, never believed in the Sith'ari prophecy, or any prophecy since he considered prophecies "wishful thinking", he nonetheless saw no reason to not claim the title figuring that it ultimately fit him.<ref name="BoSSftDS" /> [[32 BBY/Legends|Almost a century later]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] proclaimed himself to be the Sith'ari while killing his master, [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], in his sleep.<ref name="DP" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ever since its first mention, fans have speculated who the Sith'ari was. Some of the most notable candidates among this speculation were [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].<ref name="Discussion">{{WookCite|url=4400000000003642266|text=Chosen by Darkness: The Sith'ari|forum=1}}</ref><ref name="obsidian">{{WebCite|url=https://forums.obsidian.net/topic/23932-who-is-the-sithari/|text=WHO IS THE SITH'ARI?|work=[[Obsidian Entertainment|Obsidian Entertainment's]] [https://forums.obsidian.net/ official forums]|archivedate=20251202180131}}</ref><ref name="lucasforums">{{WebCite|url=https://lucasforumsarchive.com/thread/155382-revan-and-the-legend-of-the-sithari|text=Revan and the Legend of the Sith'ari|work=[[LucasArts|LucasArts's]] [https://lucasforumsarchive.com official forums]|archivedate=20251202192543}}</ref><ref name="TORforums">{{TORweb|subdomain=forums|url=topic/703675-who-is-the-real-sithari|text=Who is the real Sith'ari?}} </ref><ref name="reddit1">{{Reddit|url=r/MawInstallation/comments/qgseq6/discussion_what_if_the_sithari_wasnt_what_you|thread=[DISCUSSION] What If...? The Sith'ari Wasn't What You Thought It Was.|archivedate=20211027090613}}</ref><ref name="reddit2">{{Reddit|url=r/MawInstallation/comments/mwv2bu/sidious_sithari|thread=Sidious {{=}} Sith'ari ?|archivedate=20210423131857}}</ref> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', however, establishes Bane as being the looked-for Sith'ari, confirming the assumptions of many fans.<ref name="TCSWE" /> But the title has also been interpreted as having multiple holders throughout galactic history. Giving credence to this, the [[2012]] publication ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'' featured a number of references to the prophecy of the Sith'ari in what was intended by the book's author, [[Daniel Wallace]], to be a running joke, whereby each in-universe writer of the ''Book of Sith'' came to the conclusion that he or she was the Sith'ari.<ref name="Book of Sith endnotes">{{OfficialBlog|url=2012/10/01/star-wars-reads-day-special-book-of-sith-endnotes|text=Official Endnotes for Star Wars Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side}}</ref>
